title: Bidirectional A* on Singapore: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* route across a real city graph by expanding from the start and goal at the same time. It meets in the middle to cut search time—exactly how routing AI can feel “instant” on fast networks.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — how autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

In this visualization, the algorithm runs two A* searches simultaneously:
➡️ Forward: start → toward goal
➡️ Backward: goal → toward start
When the frontiers meet, the combined cost gives the shortest path.

Why it’s faster (the key idea):
• A* is efficient when the heuristic is good, but still expands a lot in large graphs.
• Bidirectional A* reduces the explored area by meeting in the middle, so fewer nodes get evaluated.

Takeaway: if you can safely reverse the search (or model it symmetrically), bidirectional planning often slashes the runtime.

Debate question: Should routing systems always prefer bidirectional search, or only when traffic/graph conditions stay stable?
